searchText: out of interest, will the test ceremony output be used for any of the public testnets like sepolia or goerli? <CarlBeek> > <CarlBeek> Thanks for bringing this up @jsign, I fixed these URLs in https://github.com/ethereum/kzg-ceremony-specs/pull/44 (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <ignacio (jsign)> [reply]: <@420951281910284289> , yes, I got it from the apiSpec yaml file: https://github.com/ethereum/kzg-ceremony-specs/blob/af0f7f39dc4096c8446dab1f6e7d2d5657663997/apiSpec/sequencerApi.yml#L13 So both URLs listed there should probably be deleted and we should add https://sequencer.ceremony.ethereum.org If you want I can create a PR to change it (if that's the correct change).) <CarlBeek> Heads up: I just reset the sequencer & its transcript & re-enabled the min-nonce check and disabled multi-contributions again. This is so we can test all the checking infrastructure as well as the reset process. I wil re-enable multi-contribution later this week I was able to contribute using the same tau (and by consequence the same potPubKey) in all of the 4 sub-ceremony contributions. Is this the expected behavior from the Sequencer? (I ask this because some days ago there was a conversation in this chat mentioning that potPubKeys should be different for each one of the four sub-ceremony contributions) > I am having troubles to contribute using Ethereum address. I tried Metamask and Frame with multiple addresses with history but after signing in Sign-In with Ethereum I am always redirected back on the home page and URL contains an error ?code=AuthErrorPayload%3A%3AUserCreatedAfterDeadline&error=user+created+after+deadline. No issues using Github another error sent to me after the reset, assuming this is related? maybe we need better error messages <CarlBeek> yeah, error handling seems to be poorly handled right now. my understanding <@992497067878518875> <@405860945018093609> is that we have custom error handling & messages, but they don't come up for me in either FF/chrome/safari <nicoserranop> I will check out the error handling right away 😊. @CarlBeek what is the min-nonce check date and how many txs do a wallet need? <Marcin> > <Marcin> There's nothing technically stopping you from using the same tau for all sub-ceremonies (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <arnaucube> [reply]: I was able to contribute using the same tau (and by consequence the same potPubKey) in all of the 4 sub-ceremony contributions. Is this the expected behavior from the Sequencer? (I ask this because some days ago there was a conversation in this chat mentioning that potPubKeys should be different for each one of the four sub-ceremony contributions)) <Marcin> the discussion above concerned an issue where you'd get the same pot pubkeys despite using different taus oh cool! thanks for the clarification ^^ <CarlBeek> but please do use different taus for your own implementation, it is important for the security assumptions of the ceremony perfect, yes, I updated the implementation this morning when I became aware that the taus were not different (as a sidenote, I saw it thanks to the ceremony website which displays the latest contributors with generated images for each potPubKey, really cool!, which in my case all the 4 images were the same due the tau being repeated). Thanks for the answers ^^ <Marcin> > <Marcin> Assuming we're running at the default params, you need an address with a nonce of at least 4 at block 15565180 (unless @CarlBeek has set it to something else?) (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <Trent> > I am having troubles to contribute using Ethereum address. I tried Metamask and Frame with multiple addresses with history but after signing in Sign-In with Ethereum I am always redirected back on the home page and URL contains an error ?code=AuthErrorPayload%3A%3AUserCreatedAfterDeadline&error=user+created+after+deadline. No issues using Github another error sent to me after the reset, assuming this is related? maybe we need better error messages) <CarlBeek> currently it is >=3 at block 15537393 (merge block) <@550420431744794624> , the specs currently says: > To pass the assessment, the account will require a nonce ≥ 3 on mainnet at block height 14500000 (Around 1 Apr 2022). https://github.com/ethereum/kzg-ceremony-specs/blob/master/docs/sequencer/contributorQualification.md#authentication-by-ethereum-account Surfacing just in case (not sure if 15537393 is temporary, or maybe the spec should change) Hey, while going the extra mile in my client to verify the transcript (not mandatory, but I was tempted), I got into a rabit hole reg ECDSA EIP-712. The worst case conclusion from this situation is that the sequencer might be generating wrong ECDSA signatures (!), the best case conclusion is that there might be a bug in `go-ethereum` logic. I did a more detailed explanation of this situation which ended up being too long to share in Discord. But it is not saying that the JSON attribute should be first letter uppercase. I think the standard in JSON attributes is to have the first letter in lowercase. Therefore I am inclined that a change in `go-ethereum` to accept first letter lowercase might be the solution. The worst case conclusion from this situation is that the sequencer might be generating wrong ECDSA signatures (!), the best case conclusion is that there might be a bug in `go-ethereum` logic. I did a more detailed explanation of this situation which ended up being too long to share in Discord. Please see here: https://hackmd.io/@jsign/kzg-ceremony-eip712-problem) <CarlBeek> > <CarlBeek> yup definitely should be cleaned up, thanks (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <ignacio (jsign)> <@550420431744794624> , the specs currently says: > To pass the assessment, the account will require a nonce ≥ 3 on mainnet at block height 14500000 (Around 1 Apr 2022). https://github.com/ethereum/kzg-ceremony-specs/blob/master/docs/sequencer/contributorQualification.md#authentication-by-ethereum-account Surfacing just in case (not sure if 15537393 is temporary, or maybe the spec should change)) <CarlBeek> Thanks for the detailed write-up @jsign! Definitely something worth looking into, the check in geth seems strange to me given the lack of the requirement in the EIP, but I also think it should be capitalised in the file to better match typing patterns. I need to do a bit of thinking as to whether to change the type name as doing so would break signatures on the post-audited (but not further updated) version of the front-end.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
Hey, while going the extra mile in my client to verify the transcript (not mandatory, but I was tempted), I got into a rabit hole reg ECDSA EIP-712.
The worst case conclusion from this situation is that the sequencer might be generating wrong ECDSA signatures (!), the best case conclusion is that there might be a bug in `go-ethereum` logic.

I did a more detailed explanation of this situation which ended up being too long to share in Discord.
Please see here: https://hackmd.io/@jsign/kzg-ceremony-eip712-problem

But it is not saying that the JSON attribute should be first letter uppercase. I think the standard in JSON attributes is to have the first letter in lowercase.

Therefore I am inclined that a change in `go-ethereum` to accept first letter lowercase might be the solution.
